key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence non-destructively reveals depth-dependent UV damage concentrated near the buried hole-transport-layer interface in p-i-n perovskite solar cells.
engineering_relevance: Depth-sensitive optical screening can guide interface design, with 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane modification reducing buried-interface damage and improving UV stability.
method: Use wavelength-dependent absorption to probe different depths.
Compare wide-field PL, time-resolved PL, and ideality factors under different excitation wavelengths.
UV-soak perovskite films and devices with different ITO surface modifiers.
evidence_signal: Non-destructive measurements localized preferential UV degradation at the HTL interface, consistent with ex-situ destructive tests, and showed improved stability with interface modification.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative stability gains or depth resolution, and broader operational durability beyond UV soaking remains unestablished.
paper_title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors
